answer: One defence is a stake-bonded identity vault: before an agent can trade, it must lock a refundable deposit in a vault, released only after a history of honest work. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but creating ten thousand means funding ten thousand deposits, so the attacker's cost grows with every clone while an honest agent pays once. Even at the nadir of market activity, when fees are low, that locked capital cannot be reused elsewhere, and a willow-like system that bends under spam yet keeps its bonded identities rooted stays hard to flood without paying the full price of the flood.
